install_guide.title: Overview: Installing Glimpse Alpha
install_guide.body_html:
Glimpse Alpha (formerly known as Sorakaze) is the group of Fabric mods installed on the Sorakazekarasu server. It's made up of 8 independent mods, each of which can be installed and updated separately. It doesn't replace or remove vanilla (unmodded) content like bows or minecarts — instead, it adds new items, blocks, and dimensions.

ModWhat it adds
GunsRanged weapons vanilla doesn't have (Assault Rifle, Shotgun, Sniper Rifle, and more)
RailA train that gradually speeds up, plus couplable passenger and freight cars
Building & DecorCity-building materials like traffic lights and guardrails, plus appliances like security cameras, ATMs, and elevators
VehiclesCars, buses, aircraft, and more
BossPowerful bosses to fight, and their dedicated drops
SkyA new dimension called "Sky," and the angel city and kingdom that live there
SurvivalNew ores, armor, and life-support features like temperature and the seasons
PowerPower generation and transmission networks, plus electric devices

For a detailed list of each mod's items and recipes, see the Recipes page; for what's changed so far, see the Changelog.

You need "Fabric" to use mods

Fabric is the foundation that lets Minecraft load mods. Think of it like needing a game console's base system before you can install any software on it — before installing the mods themselves, you first need to install Fabric on both the server and each player's PC.

⚠ The single easiest thing to get wrong

Mods need to be installed not just on the server, but on the PC of every single person playing. Installing them on the server does not automatically apply them to everyone. Unless the server and every player have matching Minecraft versions, Fabric, and mods, no one can join the server.

Who needs to set up what

  • The server (the Sorakazekarasu server) — Fabric server + Fabric API + the 8 Glimpse Alpha mods
  • Each individual player's PC — Fabric client + Fabric API + the 8 Glimpse Alpha mods (must exactly match the server's combination)
This site doesn't distribute the mods themselves

This site only hosts "reading material" — recipe tables, changelogs, install instructions, and the like. It does not distribute the mods themselves (the jar files). Please get the full set of jar files you need from your server admin.

How this page is organized

This guide is split into two audiences. Most people only need to read the chapter for players to be able to join. If you're the one running or administering the server yourself, please also read on to the chapter for server admins.

Currently supported versions (as of writing)

The values below reflect this page as of writing. The actual numbers change with every update, so always check the Changelog, the Recipes page, or your server admin for the current values.

ItemCurrent value
Minecraft version26.2
Required JavaJava 25 (Temurin 25 (LTS) recommended)
Fabric APIWhichever build matches your Minecraft version (e.g. fabric-api-0.154.2+26.2.jar)
Mod lineup8 mods (Guns, Rail, Building/Decor, Vehicles, Boss, Sky, Survival, Power)

install_guide.title: For Players: Setting Up to Join the Server
install_guide.body_html:
This covers what to set up if you're joining someone else's server to play. No technical expertise required. Follow the steps in order and it should take about 15-20 minutes.

Only 3 things to do
  • ① Install Fabric (the foundation that loads mods) on your PC
  • ② Put the set of mod files you got from the server admin into the right folder
  • ③ Change one launch setting and join the server

What you'll need

  • A Windows or Mac PC that can run Minecraft: Java Edition
  • The full mod set from your server admin (9 jar files = 1 Fabric API + the 8 Glimpse Alpha mods)
🛑 Very important

You can't join unless you have the exact same version and exact same mod files as the server. This page uses Minecraft version 26.2 as an example, but if your server admin gave you a different number, use that instead. Please don't double-click to open the jar files you received — just placing them in the folder is all you need to do.

Files you'll likely receive (example)

You'll get roughly these 9 files from your server admin (the version numbers change with every update).

Filename (example)What it is
fabric-api-0.154.2+26.2.jarShared components that make the mods run
glimpse-alpha-guns-…+mc26.2.jarGuns mod
glimpse-alpha-rail-…+mc26.2.jarRail mod
glimpse-alpha-deco-…+mc26.2.jarBuilding & Decor mod
glimpse-alpha-vehicles-…+mc26.2.jarVehicles mod
glimpse-alpha-boss-…+mc26.2.jarBoss mod
glimpse-alpha-sky-…+mc26.2.jarSky mod
glimpse-alpha-survival-…+mc26.2.jarSurvival mod
glimpse-alpha-power-…+mc26.2.jarPower mod

① Install Fabric

Open https://fabricmc.net/use/installer/ and get the installer. Stay on the "Client" tab (don't switch to "Server"), pick the same Minecraft Version as your server, and click "Install."

On Windows

  1. Download the installer from a button like "Download installer (Windows/.exe)" on the page, then double-click it to run it (if you see "Windows protected your PC," click "More info" → "Run anyway").
  2. Staying on the "Client" tab, pick 26.2 (the same number as your server) for Minecraft Version, leave Loader Version as-is, and click "Install."

On Mac

  1. Download the installer (.jar) via the "Download universal jar" button. There's no Mac executable (.exe).
  2. For the downloaded fabric-installer-….jar, don't just double-click it — right-click it (or control-click) and choose "Open." If you get a warning, click "Open" again.
  3. Staying on the "Client" tab, pick the same Minecraft Version as your server and click "Install."
⚠ If your Mac says "cannot verify the developer"

On recent versions of macOS, even right-click → "Open" may not show a button, and you might just see a warning saying "'fabric-installer….jar' cannot be checked for malicious software." If that happens, you can open it this way instead:

  1. Click "Done" on the warning (never click "Move to Trash")
  2. Open the Apple menu (top left) → "System Settings" → "Privacy & Security"
  3. Scroll down to find a message saying "'fabric-installer….jar' was blocked," and click "Open Anyway" next to it
  4. If asked again, click "Open Anyway" → enter your Mac password (or use Touch ID)

This is the standard warning macOS shows for anything not registered with Apple, and it's nothing to worry about as long as you got it from the official Fabric site. Once you allow it, it'll open normally from then on.

If nothing happens when you run the installer on Mac

If right-click → "Open" does nothing at all, Java isn't installed on your system. Go to adoptium.net, install the macOS installer (.pkg) for "Temurin," and try again. Choose "aarch64" for Apple Silicon Macs (M1/M2/M3/M4, etc.) or "x64" for Intel Macs. If you're not sure which, check the "Chip" field under the Apple menu (top left) → "About This Mac" (if it says "Apple M…," you want aarch64).

② Put the mod files in the mods folder

Windows: %appdata%\.minecraft\mods

  1. Type %appdata%\.minecraft into File Explorer's address bar and press Enter.
  2. If there's no mods folder, create one (all lowercase).
  3. Copy all 9 jar files you received into this mods folder (no need to unzip — drop the jars in as-is).

Mac: ~/Library/Application Support/minecraft/mods

  1. Click the desktop once, then press ⌘ command+⇧ shift+G together (or use the menu bar's "Go" → "Go to Folder…").
  2. Paste ~/Library/Application Support/minecraft exactly as-is into the box that appears and press Enter (don't forget the leading "~"). "Library" is normally hidden in Finder, so this is the reliable way to get there.
  3. If there's no mods folder, right-click in that window and choose "New Folder" to create one.
  4. Drag and drop all 9 jar files you received into this mods folder.

③ Launch with Fabric and join the server

  1. Open the Minecraft launcher and, from the list of launch profiles near the "Play" button, pick something named like fabric-loader-26.2 (staying on "Latest Release" will launch without any mods).
  2. Click "Play" to launch as usual. If a "Mods" button has appeared on the title screen, it worked — clicking it will show all 8 Glimpse Alpha mods plus Fabric API.
  3. From there, connect to the server through "Multiplayer" as usual.

When the mods get updated

Whenever the server-side mods are updated, everyone joining needs to update to the same version at the same time.

  1. Get the new mod files from your server admin (wait for their announcement before doing this).
  2. Open your mods folder, delete the Glimpse Alpha jar files that were there before, then add the new ones (even if the filenames changed, they're treated as the same mod — leaving old ones in place will prevent launch).
  3. Launch with the fabric-loader profile as usual.
⚠ Note

If only one side is on the new version, you won't be able to join. If you get stuck, check the FAQ too.

Common Mac hiccups

SymptomFix
Says "cannot verify the developer" / "cannot be checked for malicious software"Click "Done" on the warning (not "Move to Trash"). Then scroll down in System Settings → "Privacy & Security" and click "Open Anyway" next to the "was blocked" message, then enter your password.
Nothing happens when double-clicking the installerJava isn't installed. Get Temurin (macOS .pkg) from adoptium.net and try again.
Can't find the "Library" folderNo need to hunt for it manually. Press ⌘+⇧+G and paste in ~/Library/Application Support/minecraft — this is the reliable way (it's normally a hidden folder).
Told there's a version mismatch when trying to join the serverCheck ① that you've selected the correct fabric-loader profile in the launcher, and ② that your mods folder matches the server's exactly. Even one mismatch will prevent you from joining.
Crashes the instant it launchesCheck your mods folder for old or unrelated jar files mixed in. If that doesn't fix it, send logs/latest.log (on Mac: ~/Library/Application Support/minecraft/logs/latest.log) to your server admin.
Want to go back to plain Minecraft with no modsJust switch the launcher's profile back to "Latest Release." No need to delete the mod files.

The steps are the same whether you're on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4, etc.) or an Intel Mac — the only difference is picking aarch64 vs. x64 when choosing Java (Temurin).

install_guide.title: For Server Admins: Preparation (Backup & Version Check)
install_guide.body_html:
From here on, this chapter is for whoever runs and administers the server itself. It walks through adding Fabric and the 8 Glimpse Alpha mods to a Minecraft server that's already running vanilla (a standard, unmodded server). This chapter uses a Windows server as its example. If you're running your server on Mac / Linux, translate the folder locations and command steps to your own environment and follow the same general process (per the official Fabric site's instructions).

🛑 Before you do anything

Always take a backup before you start, so a failed mod install can't cost you your world.

1. Back up your world

Open your server's folder (e.g. C:\MinecraftServer) and run whatever backup process you normally use (e.g. a backup script like Backup-Server.bat). If you don't have a dedicated script, it's fine to just stop the server and copy the entire world folder somewhere else.

2. Check your Java version

  1. Open Command Prompt (or any terminal).
  2. Type java -version and press Enter.
  3. Check whether the number shown is 25 (e.g. java version "25.0.3").
🛑 Very important

Running Minecraft 26.2 requires Java 25. Older setup instructions sometimes say "Java 21," but that's outdated — the server won't start with Java 21. If your number is below 25, go to adoptium.net, download and install "Temurin 25 (LTS)," restart your computer, and check again.

3. Check the server's Minecraft version

  1. Start the server up once, the way you normally would (e.g. Start-Server.bat).
  2. Look near the top of the console (the black window) for a line like Starting minecraft server version X.Y, and note the number.
  3. Type stop in the console and press Enter to safely shut the server down.
⚠ Note

This guide uses "26.2" as its example, but if the number you actually found is different, use that number in every step from here on (when selecting Fabric, Fabric API, and mod versions). If the server, every player, and the mods don't all match on version, nothing will work at all.

install_guide.title: For Server Admins: Installing Fabric
install_guide.body_html:
Install the Fabric server

  1. Open https://fabricmc.net/use/server/ in your browser and download the installer from a button like "Download installer (Windows/.exe)."
  2. Double-click the downloaded fabric-installer….exe to launch it (if you see "Windows protected your PC," click "More info" → "Run anyway").
  3. On the installer's settings screen, check these 4 things:
    • Select the "Server" tab
    • Set Minecraft Version to match the server version you confirmed earlier (e.g. 26.2)
    • Loader Version can stay as-is
    • Set Install Location to your existing server folder (e.g. C:\MinecraftServer)
  4. Click "Install."
  5. If a new file called fabric-server-launch.jar now exists in your server folder, it worked.

Create a new launch file (batch file)

Your existing launch file (e.g. Start-Server.bat) launches the server "without mods." Leave it in place (so you can go back to a mod-free server if you ever need to). Instead, create a new launch file for Fabric.

  1. Open Notepad.
  2. Copy and paste in the following as-is: 
    @echo off
cd /d "%~dp0"
title Minecraft Fabric Server
java -Xms2G -Xmx4G -jar fabric-server-launch.jar nogui
echo Server stopped.
pause
  3. Choose "File" → "Save As," and save it to your server folder (e.g. C:\MinecraftServer) with the filename Start-Fabric-Server.bat, setting "Save as type" to "All Files."
⚠ Note

If you don't set "Save as type" to "All Files," you'll end up with a non-functional file named Start-Fabric-Server.bat.txt. Also, if your server was set up with a memory (RAM) allocation other than 4GB, change the "4" in -Xmx4G to match.

install_guide.title: For Server Admins: Installing the Mods & Verifying Startup
install_guide.body_html:
Each mod is a single file called a "jar" file. You install it just by putting it in your server folder's mods folder.

1. Set up the mods folder

Check whether your server folder (e.g. C:\MinecraftServer) has a folder named mods. If not, right-click → "New" → "Folder" and name it mods (all lowercase).

2. Get Fabric API

Open https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api/versions and download the topmost entry whose "Game version" matches your server (e.g. fabric-api-0.154.2+26.2.jar).

3. Put the full mod set in the mods folder

Copy all 9 jar files — 1 Fabric API + the 8 Glimpse Alpha mods — into the mods folder (no need to unzip — drop the jars in as-is). Get the 8 mods themselves through whatever distribution channel you've been using. This site does not distribute the mods themselves.

ModExample filename
Gunsglimpse-alpha-guns-…+mc26.2.jar
Railglimpse-alpha-rail-…+mc26.2.jar
Building & Decorglimpse-alpha-deco-…+mc26.2.jar
Vehiclesglimpse-alpha-vehicles-…+mc26.2.jar
Bossglimpse-alpha-boss-…+mc26.2.jar
Skyglimpse-alpha-sky-…+mc26.2.jar
Survivalglimpse-alpha-survival-…+mc26.2.jar
Powerglimpse-alpha-power-…+mc26.2.jar
⚠ Note

Don't double-click the jar files (no need to open them). Just placing them in the folder is enough.

4. Start the server and verify it

  1. Double-click the Start-Fabric-Server.bat you just created (don't use the old Start-Server.bat).
  2. In the console (the black window), check these 2 things:
    • The names of the mods you installed appear in the mod-loading lines
    • It ends with Done (…s)! For help, type "help" and keeps running without stopping
💡 If a Java error stops it from starting

If you see an English error like "class file version" or "requires Java," your Java may be too old. Install the Windows version (.msi) of "Temurin 25 (LTS)" from adoptium.net, restart your computer, and try again.

Once you've confirmed it starts up, walk everyone joining through the chapter for players so they can install the same Fabric and mod set on their own PCs.

install_guide.title: Updating to a New Mod Version
install_guide.body_html:
Since Glimpse Alpha's 8 mods are each fully independent, an update doesn't necessarily mean all 8 get replaced. You only need to swap out the mods whose contents actually changed (check the distribution notes or the Changelog to see which mods were touched).

Update steps

  1. Type stop in the server console to shut it down.
  2. Back up your world using your usual backup process.
  3. In the server's mods folder, delete the old jar file(s) for the mods being updated, then add the new jar file(s) (having both old and new versions of the same mod present will prevent startup).
  4. Start the server with Start-Fabric-Server.bat and confirm the console shows the updated version.
  5. Distribute the new jar files to everyone joining and have them swap them out the same way (see the chapter for players). No one can join if only the server or only players are on the new version.
🛑 Very important

If you start the server with a mod completely removed (rather than just updated), any blocks placed or items held that belong to that mod (like traffic lights) will disappear. This is how Minecraft and Fabric work, and it can't be undone. Always back up before removing a mod.

About config files (the auto-repair mechanism)

Every mod automatically generates a config file (e.g. sorakaze_guns.json) inside the config/ folder on startup. You can adjust values like damage and speed there, and you generally never need to manually delete or edit it with each update.

💡 How it currently works

When a new release changes a default value, it's automatically updated to the new default only for settings you haven't touched yet (ones still sitting at an old default). Values you've tuned yourself are never touched. Newly added settings are also automatically appended on startup. Whatever gets updated is always logged in logs/latest.log as "old value → new value."

⚠ Note on editing config files by hand

If you manually delete just part of a value inside a config file (e.g. removing only the damage line from one weapon's settings block), that item can silently fall back to a different internal default from inside the mod itself (with no error shown). If you want to adjust a specific number, edit that value directly instead. If you want to reset a mod's settings to defaults entirely, delete that mod's whole config file — it'll be rebuilt with defaults the next time the server starts.

install_guide.title: Things to Know Before You Play
install_guide.body_html:
Glimpse Alpha includes a handful of changes that affect vanilla behavior. This section covers the ones that are especially easy to miss. Since fine details can be adjusted with any update, also check the Changelog and Known Issues pages for the latest status. Config adjustments are something your server admin handles.

Redstone now needs "electricity"

With the Power mod installed, part of vanilla redstone no longer works on its own.

  • Now requires electricity: redstone dust, repeaters, comparators, redstone blocks, and redstone torches. None of these will output a signal until they're wired to electricity via cable. Auto-farms, stations, automatic doors, and hopper lines will all stay shut down until you wire them up.
  • Still work without electricity, as before: levers, buttons, pressure plates, tripwire hooks, observers, daylight sensors, sculk sensors, targets, trapped chests, detector rails, lecterns, jukeboxes, lightning rods, and more. Manually opening doors and gates also works as usual.
  • A redstone block naturally breaks about 10 minutes after being placed (returning to your inventory as an item).
💡 How to revert this (for server admins)

Setting powerEnabled to false in config/sorakaze_power.json disables redstone electrification entirely.

Some Building & Decor devices also need electricity

5 devices — the security camera, elevator, escalator, automatic door, and ATM — won't work unless they have electricity wired in via cable (the elevator still works "going down" even without power). Setting the corresponding option to false in config/sorakaze_deco.json lets you make electricity optional for each one individually.

Generators heat up rooms

Running generators and nuclear plants raise the temperature of the space they're in. Only air conditioners can cool it back down. Sectioning off your machine room with walls and a closed door is an easy way to keep the heat from spreading to other rooms. This feature itself can be disabled by setting temperatureMachineHeatEnabled to false in config/sorakaze_survival.json.

The Sky world's height has been extended

With the Sky mod installed, the maximum build height in the Overworld has been raised. Only the upper limit changes — the depth underground (the bottom of the world) and existing terrain are unaffected.

The Rocket Launcher destroys terrain

By default, the Guns mod's Rocket Launcher destroys terrain at its point of impact. Setting the vanilla game rule mobGriefing to false does not stop this. To stop the destruction, you need to set rocketDestroysTerrain to false in config/sorakaze_guns.json. Be especially careful near your base.

About gun damage

The Guns mod's weapons — especially the Assault Rifle — deal extremely high damage, and many of the mod-added bosses can be killed in a matter of seconds. If you want more of a challenge, your server admin can restore the difficulty by adjusting each weapon's damage value in config/sorakaze_guns.json.

Removing a mod deletes any blocks/items it added

This is how mods work in general, not a bug specific to Glimpse Alpha. Any blocks placed or items obtained while a mod was installed will be lost from the world if that mod is removed. The only way to undo this is to restore from a backup.

install_guide.title: FAQ & Troubleshooting
install_guide.body_html:
Frequently asked questions

QuestionAnswer
Will my world get deleted?No. Installing Fabric doesn't touch your existing world — it keeps working as-is. If you're worried, always take a backup before installing.
Can a friend without the mods join?No. Every player needs to complete the setup in the chapter for players.
I want to go back to no mods (vanilla)On the server side, just launch with your original no-mods launch file to go back to vanilla (any blocks/items added by the mods will disappear).
Updating the mods suddenly broke thingsCheck whether the mod versions match between the server and players. You can't join if only one side is on the new version.
I don't understand the error messageThat's fine — you don't need to. Just send the latest.log file, found inside the logs folder, directly to your server admin as-is.

If the server won't start

  1. Temporarily move everything out of the mods folder to somewhere else.
  2. Add files back one at a time, restarting each time, to find out which one is causing the problem.
  3. If you see Java-related errors, check your Java version — see the preparation chapter.

If you can reach the server but can't connect

  1. Check whether every player's version and mod set exactly matches the server's.
  2. Mismatched Fabric API versions are an especially common culprit, so check that first.
💡 If nothing fixes it

Send logs/latest.log to your server admin and ask for help. No need to panic — as long as you have a backup, you can always get back to where you were.

How to restore a world from backup (for server admins)

  1. Type stop in the server console to shut it down.
  2. Grab the most recent backup from wherever they're stored (e.g. C:\MinecraftServer\backups) (if it's a zip, right-click → "Extract All").
  3. Swap the extracted world folder in for the world folder inside your server folder (overwriting it).
  4. Start the server.

howto.title: How to Use Auto-Sorting
howto.lede: Build a storage system that decides where to put things for you. No complicated wiring required — start by building just ① first.

sections.title: ① Start with just one
sections.goal: Get only coal to end up in the box on the right. This is the foundation for everything else.

diagram.caption: Pulls from the box behind it and puts items in the box in front (side view)
rows: Box that only fills with coal

steps: Place a box, a Sorting Filter, and a box, touching each other in that order.
Place the Sorting Filter so its front (the colored face) points toward the box you want items to go into.
Hold coal in your hand and right-click the Sorting Filter. This teaches it to "let coal through" (it won't consume the coal you're holding).
That's it. No matter what you put in the box on the left, only coal will move into the box on the right.
notes: If you haven't registered any sample yet, nothing will pass through (it's not broken).
To clear a registration, hold the same item and right-click again. To clear everything, sneak+right-click. Right-clicking empty-handed shows the current list.

sections.title: ② Line them up to build a sorting yard
sections.goal: Route a single line out into separate boxes by item type. This is where it starts feeling like a real warehouse.

diagram.caption: Items flow along the top line and drop down to be sorted (side view)

out: Not registered, so it flows all the way to the end

steps: Build your trunk line (the main flow) out of Item Pumps. They're faster than hoppers and move a whole stack at once, so they don't clog.
Place one downward-facing Sorting Filter for each type you want to sort, and register a sample on each.
Placing a Void Trash at the very end deletes anything that didn't make it into any box. If there's something you don't want thrown away, put a regular box there instead.
notes: The Void Trash also only deletes items you've registered as samples. Just placing it does nothing on its own, so it's safe to place it before configuring it.

sections.title: ③ Too many types? Split them broadly first
sections.goal: Registering 40 kinds of food one by one is a hassle. Sort them in bulk instead.

diagram.caption: 8 categories (food, tools, ores, farming, redstone, fuel, building materials, other)

steps: Place a Category Sorter. It's placed the same way as a Sorting Filter.
Right-click it empty-handed to cycle through categories. Keep clicking until you land on the one you want.
No sample registration needed. Anything matching the category passes through as a group.
notes: If you need finer sorting, add a Sorting Filter after this (split broadly first, then refine).

sections.title: ④ Run several furnaces at once
sections.goal: Distribute a single line evenly across 5 furnaces.

diagram.caption: Deals out one item at a time, in turn, to whatever containers are touching the splitter

steps: Place furnaces (or boxes) touching the Round-Robin Splitter on all sides.
All 5 faces other than the input side become output destinations.
No sample registration needed. It just hands out whatever comes in, in turn.

sections.title: ⑤ Keep things running even when a box is full
sections.goal: Normally, a full destination box backs up your entire sorting yard. This prevents that.

diagram.caption: Diverts to the side only when the front is full

steps: Place an Overflow Valve right before your usual destination.
Place a box to the side (or above/below) to catch the overflow.
No configuration needed. It automatically diverts sideways only when the front is full.

sections.title: ⑥ Counting, checking stock, and copying settings
sections.goal: Tools for checking whether things are working, and for copying the same settings to multiple machines.

diagram.caption: Left: counts items passing through / Middle: outputs remaining stock as a redstone signal / Right: copies and pastes settings
rows: Picks up dropped items and stores them

steps: Place the Item Counter in the middle of a line. It lets items pass straight through while counting them, and outputs the count to a comparator (right-click for the running total, sneak+right-click to reset to 0).

The Stock Indicator doesn't move any items. It reads the stock in the box in front of it, lights up once it passes a threshold, and outputs that same value to a comparator — letting you wire a distant warehouse's stock level into your redstone.
The Item Collector sucks in dropped items from the surrounding area and puts them in the box in front of it. Handy for picking up drops from a farm.

The Filter Card copies a Sorting Filter's settings when you right-click it with a blank card, and pastes them when you right-click with a loaded card. You can copy the same settings to as many machines as you like (right-click in midair to erase a card).

howto.title: How to Wire Up Electricity
howto.lede: Electricity is just "generate → transmit → distribute → use" — that's the whole thing. Start by lining up 4 devices exactly as shown in diagram ①. A Breaker Panel finishes setting itself up just by being placed (no need to open any settings screen). ⚠ Installing this mod also means redstone needs electricity too — make sure to read ⑩.

sections.title: ① The flow of electricity (start here)
sections.goal: Generator, cable, breaker panel, device — those 4 things are the whole of electricity.

diagram.caption: Fuel → generator → cable → breaker panel → cable → device (this runs wide, so scroll it sideways with your finger or mouse)

steps: Place a Generator. Just placing the single item grows a 4×4×5 structure on its own (no assembly required). It can't be placed in a cramped spot, so leave room around it.
Hold coal and right-click the generator to feed it fuel. It'll light up.
Run Cable from the generator to a Breaker Panel. The generator can be connected from any face.

Run Cable from the breaker panel to whichever device you want to power. There's nothing to configure here. The breaker panel decides the circuit, voltage, and capacity for itself the moment it's placed.
If a cable is lit up, it's carrying power. Anywhere a cable isn't lit, electricity isn't reaching.
notes: A generator only produces electricity, and a breaker panel only distributes it. Neither works alone — you need both.
If something's not working, first trace whether the cables are lit with your eyes. Wherever the light stops is where the problem is.
The Nuclear Plant works a bit differently — it doesn't power a breaker panel directly. Instead it produces Energy Cells, which get sent to a breaker panel via cable (see ⑤).

"Machine Casing" and "Reactor Shielding" aren't used for assembly anymore. They're leftover parts from when machines had to be built up by hand, and they're kept around now purely as sturdy decorative blocks (so anything you'd already built with them doesn't disappear). You don't need to buy any more of them.

sections.title: ② 4 kinds of cable — which one do you need?
sections.goal: There are 2 separate axes to choose on: thickness = how far it reaches, and banding = whether it can carry high voltage. These are independent of each other, so there's no single "best" cable.

diagram.caption: The thicker it is, the farther it reaches. Only cables with banding at the joints can carry high voltage (at default settings)

steps: Start by running Regular Cable. If it lights up, that's all you need.

If the light fades out partway, you're out of range. Either switch to a thicker cable or raise the voltage (③). Taking Regular Cable's range as 1, Insulated Cable reaches 2x as far, Heavy-gauge Cable 4x, and Shielded Cable 8x.

Only Insulated Cable or Shielded Cable can carry high voltage (6,600V). If you set Regular Cable to high voltage, the breaker panel will show "insufficient insulation" and refuse to run (it won't silently break).
notes: ⚠ Heavy-gauge Cable is not an "upgrade" over Insulated Cable. Heavy-gauge Cable has a thicker conductor (= reaches farther at low voltage), but it can't carry high voltage. Conversely, Insulated Cable can carry high voltage, but loses out to Heavy-gauge Cable on low-voltage range. Only reach for Shielded Cable when you need both (it's the most expensive, so there's no reason to buy it otherwise).

You only need high-voltage-rated cable for the stretch between the breaker panel and the transformer. Past the transformer, it steps down to 200V, so cheap Regular Cable is the right call from there to your devices (the same idea as a real-world transformer on a utility pole).
A single breaker panel can trace out to 512 cable blocks at most. For a bigger base than that, split it across 2 breaker panels.
The distances above come from the rule "up to the point where 10% of the electricity is lost in transit." Beyond that, cables won't light up and devices won't run.

sections.title: ③ Breaker Panel — circuits, voltage, and amperage
sections.goal: Voltage buys you "how far it reaches." Amperage buys you "how many devices you can run at once." That one sentence is the whole story on breaker panels.

diagram.caption: Each breaker panel has 8 circuits, automatically split by each cable branch

steps: Normally, you don't need to do anything. The moment it's placed, a breaker panel has already decided its own circuits, names, voltage, and amperage.

Voltage has 3 tiers (100V / 200V / 6,600V high voltage). The higher it is, the farther it reaches — since loss is inversely proportional to the square of voltage, doubling the voltage roughly quadruples the range.
Amperage has 6 tiers: 15A / 20A / 30A / 50A / 75A / 100A. As a rough guide, 15A at 100V runs about 7 devices, and 15A at 200V runs about 15 (1 device = 200W).

Exceed capacity and only that circuit "trips" (the other circuits keep running). Open the breaker panel and flip that row back on to restore it. If it keeps happening, either raise the amperage (100A is the highest tier) or spread devices across a different circuit.
notes: Raising the voltage lowers the amperage draw. Even for the same devices, switching to 200V halves the current, making trips less likely (the same logic as real-world electrical work).
The auto-selected amperage always leaves headroom (it picks the smallest tier where actual usage stays under 80% of rating), so it won't trip the moment you place it.
Flipping off the breaker panel's "main" switch stops every circuit at once — handy when doing wiring work.

sections.title: ④ Transformer — only pays off over long distances
sections.goal: High voltage reaches far, but a transformer keeps consuming electricity even when nothing's drawing power. That makes it a net loss for short runs.

diagram.caption: Breaker panel → (high voltage, insulated) → transformer → (200V, regular cable) → device

steps: The break-even point is roughly 24 blocks. For runs shorter than that, 100V/200V wins out; for longer runs, high voltage wins out.
When going high-voltage, place a transformer near your devices. Connect from the breaker panel to the transformer with Insulated Cable.
Past the transformer, it steps down to 200V. From there to your devices, Regular Cable is fine (and cheaper).
notes: If you set high voltage without placing a transformer, the breaker panel will show "no transformer" and won't run.
If you're just connecting a nearby base, you don't need high voltage — 200V already reaches 128 blocks.

sections.title: ⑤ Fuel — anything a furnace can burn works here too
sections.goal: It'll run on anything, but how much electricity you get out varies wildly. Wood is the worst deal by far.

diagram.caption: Weakest on the left, strongest on the right (output per tick = number of devices it can run)

steps: Hold fuel and right-click to load it in. It works on the generator, the Nuclear Plant, and even the breaker panel itself.
Skip wood if you can. It only puts out 1/4 the power of coal, and burns for a shorter time too, so it's gone in no time.

Energy Cells are the strongest fuel there is (16 units = 63 devices). The Nuclear Plant makes them from coal (roughly 120 seconds per cell, and it stops once 8 are stockpiled so it doesn't waste coal).
You can also plug a cell straight into the breaker panel. One cell lasts about 10 minutes (it drains faster the more electricity you're drawing).
notes: Burning fuel directly in a breaker panel only gets you 50% of its normal duration. Treat it as an emergency backup — building a proper generator is the better deal for real power generation.
1 Coal is worth 6,400 units — enough to run 15 devices for 80 seconds.

Burning a cell as fuel only lasts 25 seconds (plugging it straight into a breaker panel lasts much longer). Since it takes the Nuclear Plant about 120 seconds to make one cell, burning cells to make more cells is a net loss.

sections.title: ⑥ Auto-feeding fuel with hoppers
sections.goal: Feeding coal by hand every time is a hassle. Hook up a hopper and it's automatic.

diagram.caption: Hopper on top = feeds in / hopper on the bottom = takes out

out: Empty buckets (from burning lava buckets) come out from below too

steps: Point a hopper into the top or side of a machine and fuel will feed in.
Place a hopper under a machine to pull out finished Energy Cells and empty buckets (from burning lava buckets).
Any cell within the 4×4×5 structure works. A hopper functions no matter where on the structure you attach it.
The same goes for the fireplace and breaker panel. The fireplace can be fed coal from the top or the side.
notes: Hoppers don't need electricity. Whether they're moving fuel or anything else, they work exactly as before.

Through v1.8.3, hoppers also needed electricity. That could create a deadlock — "no fuel gets delivered → no power gets generated → the hopper doesn't run" — so we dropped that requirement. Any hopper that was stuck will start working again automatically after you update.

sections.title: ⑦ Fuel-free power generation (3 kinds)
sections.goal: These generate power for free, but each has conditions attached. One alone won't be enough — line up several to scale up.

diagram.caption: Output drops or stops if conditions aren't met
rows: Needs open sky and daytime — 0 at night
Needs height + open space around the blades

steps: For all 3, you just connect them to a breaker panel with cable. No fuel needed.
Put the Solar Panel on a rooftop. It won't generate without a clear view of the sky. It stops at night and in the rain.
Put the Wind Turbine atop a tall tower. It barely spins at or below Y64, and reaches full power at Y160. Keep the space around its blades clear. It keeps spinning at night too.
Put the Water Flow Generator in a river. It won't run in still water (it needs flowing water). It's at full power with 4 faces touching flowing water, and stays constant day and night.
If it's not enough, just line up more of them. Output simply adds together.
notes: Every one of these is either weaker than a coal generator or comes with strict conditions. Solar only puts out half of coal's power, and drops to 0 for half the day.
Right-click it empty-handed to see what percentage it's currently generating at, or why it's stopped.

sections.title: ⑧ ⚠ Generators heat up rooms (fireplace and air conditioner)
sections.goal: A running generator heats up the room it's in. More generators means more heat, and if you leave it unchecked, you'll start taking damage. The air conditioner is the only thing that cools it back down.

diagram.caption: Effect per running machine (a stopped machine is 0°C)
rows: For cold protection / needs no electricity

out: Place one in the same room and it goes away

steps: It's counted across however far "that room's" air is connected. Wall it off with a closed door and neither heat nor cooling reaches the other side. That's why the simplest fix is just sealing off your machine room.
An air conditioner works equally well no matter where in the room you place it (distance doesn't matter). It doesn't need to sit right next to the generators.
You need 1 air conditioner for every 2.5 generators. Scale up to 2 for 4 generators, or 4 for 8 generators.
Heat is reduced to 25% outdoors. If you just can't cool a space down enough, removing the roof and going open-air is also an option.

When you want to warm up, use a fireplace. Just hold coal and right-click to feed it (a hopper on top works too), and it raises the temperature by +14°C within a 5-block radius. No electricity needed. 1 Coal lasts 80 seconds, so once the fire goes out, it stops warming things up.
notes: You get a warning above 30°C, and start losing health at 45°C or higher. If the on-screen thermometer turns red, add more air conditioners or shut down some generators.
The air conditioner won't overcool. It won't drop the temperature below 30°C, so placing one in a snowy area won't freeze you.

The air conditioner needs electricity (the fireplace doesn't). Connect it to a breaker panel with cable. It becomes a 3×2×2 structure once placed. Sneak+right-click to switch it on/off, and right-click empty-handed to check its status.
Heat caps out at 15 generators (+120°C). Adding more beyond that won't make it any hotter, but air conditioners still each pull their full weight regardless.
If overheating is a problem for you, setting temperatureMachineHeatEnabled to false in config/sorakaze_survival.json turns off machine heat specifically (air conditioners keep working).

sections.title: ⑨ ⚠ Things that now need electricity
sections.goal: Installing this mod means things that used to work will stop. Wire them up and they'll work again.

diagram.caption: None of the devices on this list will work unless they're connected to a breaker panel via cable

steps: Run Cable from a breaker panel out to wherever a device has stopped working.
If the cable is lit, it's powered. If it's not, check your breaker panel, generator, and fuel.
Each device draws 200W. Every 800W (= 4 devices) adds another unit of required generation.
notes: The Enhanced Beacon works a bit differently — it just checks whether an adjacent cable is lit.

For the Building & Decor mod's devices (camera, elevator, escalator, automatic door, ATM), you can make electricity optional for each one individually via the Building & Decor mod's own config (the …RequiresPower options in config/sorakaze_deco.json).

sections.title: ⑩ ⚠⚠ Redstone needs electricity too (the most important one)
sections.goal: Every redstone circuit in the world stops working wherever electricity isn't reaching. Farms, stations, and automatic doors that are currently running will stop too.

diagram.caption: Left: needs electricity (6 kinds) / Right: always works without electricity (21 kinds)

steps: There's only one fix. Run cable from a breaker panel to wherever that circuit is. That's all it takes to get it working again.

"Sensing" components — levers, buttons, pressure plates, observers, daylight sensors, and the like — always work even without electricity (21 kinds in total). This is so you never lose the ability to fix a powerless base from within the game.

A redstone block placed somewhere without electricity crumbles after about 10 minutes. It drops as an item when it does (you don't lose it). This prevents placing one from becoming a free source of electricity. It won't crumble in a powered location, so it's safe to use as decoration in a wired-up base.

Devices of the "stops when powered" type stay active in places without electricity. This only applies to 3 devices: the Void Trash, laser emitter, and Auto Turret. That's because a Void Trash deleting your items, or a laser/turret switching on and killing animals or villagers, is something you can't undo.

As of v1.8.3, 14 more devices were also on this list. Sorting machines, conveyor belts, traffic lights, the automatic train stop block, and more all required electricity to function — we removed every one of them from the list. They now work without electricity (any that were stuck will start working again automatically once you update).
notes: There's a way to revert all of this back to how it used to work. Set redstoneRequiresPower to false in config/sorakaze_power.json. Redstone will go back to behaving exactly as if this mod weren't installed (restart the server after switching it).
If you want to turn off the entire power system, set powerEnabled to false in the same file. Neither devices nor redstone will need electricity anymore, and no placed blocks disappear.
Vanilla hoppers are not affected. They keep working exactly as before, with or without electricity.

sections.title: ⑪ LED Panel — the brightest light there is, powered by electricity
sections.goal: Light level 15 (the maximum vanilla allows). It's a thin panel, so mounting it on a ceiling won't bump your head.

diagram.caption: 3/16 of a block thick. Sticks to any flat surface — floor, wall, or ceiling
rows: Wider and brighter than a torch

steps: Right-click the surface you want to mount it on. Its orientation is determined by the face you place it on.
Connect it to a breaker panel with cable. It won't light up without power (if it stays dark, it's not broken — it just isn't getting electricity).

Placing them edge-to-edge with no gaps extends the lit area even further. Exactly how much is spelled out with measured values in the item's tooltip (shown when you hold it), covering 3×3, 5×5, and 7×7 arrangements.
notes: It goes dark if the power fails. If you're relying on it alone to prevent mob spawns, you'll get spawns inside your base the night your fuel runs out. Keep some torches around in important spots as a backup.
It still works underwater (waterlogging it won't make it stop working).
